input: Get an allergy panel test done this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Allergy panels vary widely — food, environmental, skin, respiratory, comprehensive — and the type determines which specialist or lab to go to.
Knowing whether this is for themselves or someone else (e.g., a child) affects referral requirements, consent, and booking logistics.
Whether they already have a doctor's referral or need to get one first changes the sequence of steps entirely.
Insurance coverage or out-of-pocket budget directly determines which labs, clinics, or specialists are viable options.
Preferred location or willingness to travel affects which facilities are on the shortlist and how quickly they can get an appointment.
Whether they need results interpreted by a doctor or just raw lab results changes whether they need a follow-up appointment planned as part of this task.
Some people prefer a hospital/specialist setting while others want a quick walk-in lab — this shapes which path to recommend.

gold.taskTitle: Get an allergy panel test done this month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to schedule and complete an allergy panel test within the current month.

questions.title: Which type of allergies are you testing for?
questions.description: Identify the category of allergy panel needed — food, environmental/seasonal, skin, respiratory, or a broad comprehensive panel — to determine the right specialist or lab.

questions.title: Is this test for yourself or someone else?
questions.description: Determine who the patient is, as testing a child or another person involves different referral, consent, and booking requirements.

questions.title: Do you already have a doctor's referral for this?
questions.description: Establish whether a referral is in hand, in progress, or not yet started, since this is often the very first step before booking.

questions.title: Will you be using insurance, or paying out of pocket?
questions.description: Clarify the payment method to filter clinics and labs by what is covered or affordable, and to flag any pre-authorization steps needed.

questions.title: How far are you willing to travel for the appointment?
questions.description: Understand the geographic range the user is comfortable with to narrow down which facilities are realistically on the shortlist.

questions.title: Do you need a doctor to review and explain your results?
questions.description: Find out whether a follow-up consultation to interpret results is part of what 'done' means, or if receiving the raw lab report is sufficient.

questions.title: Do you prefer a specialist clinic or a walk-in lab?
questions.description: Gauge whether the user wants a formal allergist/specialist setting with deeper expertise, or a faster, more convenient walk-in or direct-to-consumer lab option.
